bindings.label: A 52-year-old woman presented with sudden chest tightness and then developed severe respiratory distress and cardiac arrest
Patient has a history of Sjogren's syndrome and initially presented to a regional hospital with sudden chest tightness

On day 3, the patient developed severe respiratory distress and cardiac arrest with severe ventricular arrhythmias refractory to conventional CPR; after tracheal intubation, she received V-A ECMO and IABP
On day 4, due to worsening cardiovascular status and persistent electrical instability despite V-A ECMO and IABP, the patient was transferred to another hospital by helicopter
Upon arrival, blood pressure was 83/64 mmHg while on ECMO at 3.5 L/min and IABP; bedside echocardiography showed severely depressed global wall motion with LVEF approximately 10%
Endomyocardial biopsy shows diffuse monocyte and multinucleated giant cell infiltration with myocardial necrosis and fibrosis
Troponin is markedly elevated at 14210 ng/L
Coronary angiography shows normal coronary arteries
